1. Check that the html element has a lang attribute set to a valid BCP 47 language code because screen readers need language to select correct voice.
2. Check that the page contains a <title> element in the head because title is announced by browsers and assistive tech.
3. Check that the title text is descriptive and unique per page because users need to identify page purpose.
4. Check that a meta charset declaration is present as utf-8 because character encoding prevents garbled text.
5. Check that a meta viewport tag exists with width=device-width and initial-scale=1 because viewport controls mobile scaling.
6. Check that the body element has a logical heading hierarchy starting with h1 because heading order aids navigation.
7. Check that there is exactly one h1 per page because single main heading improves outline clarity.
8. Check that heading levels do not skip e.g., h2 to h4 because skipping confuses outline navigation.
9. Check that all images have alt attributes because alt provides text alternative for non-visual users.
10. Check that decorative images have empty alt="" because empty alt hides them from screen readers.
11. Check that informative images have descriptive alt text not just filename because description conveys meaning.
12. Check that all links have discernible text because link purpose must be clear without color alone.
13. Check that link text is not generic like "click here" because generic text is ambiguous out of context.
14. Check that link focus indicator is visible with sufficient contrast because keyboard users need focus visibility.
15. Check that focus order follows DOM order because logical tab sequence is required.
16. Check that all interactive elements are reachable via keyboard Tab key because keyboard operability is mandatory.
17. Check that TabIndex is not used to create illogical order because natural order preserves predictability.
18. Check that skip navigation link is present as first focusable element because it allows bypassing repetitive content.
19. Check that skip link becomes visible on focus because hidden skip links must appear when focused.
20. Check that form labels are explicitly associated with inputs via for/id because labels enable screen reader identification.
21. Check that placeholder text is not used as sole label because placeholders disappear and are not read reliably.
22. Check that required form fields are indicated by aria-required or visual cue because users need to know mandatory fields.
23. Check that error messages are programmatically associated with inputs via aria-describedby because errors must be announced.
24. Check that input types are semantic e.g., email, tel, number because correct type enables appropriate keyboards.
25. Check that autocomplete attributes are used on forms where appropriate because autocomplete aids form filling.
26. Check that color is not the only means to convey information because colorblind users need redundant cues.
27. Check that status messages use aria-live regions because dynamic updates must be announced.
28. Check that buttons have type attribute set to button or submit because default type can cause unintended submission.
29. Check that all interactive custom widgets have role and state attributes because ARIA roles map to native semantics.
30. Check that aria-hidden is not applied to focusable elements because hidden elements should not receive focus.
31. Check that page has sufficient color contrast for normal text at least 4.5:1 because low contrast reduces readability.
32. Check that large text 18pt or 14pt bold meets 3:1 contrast because large text has relaxed requirement.
33. Check that UI components like buttons meet 3:1 contrast for non-text elements because contrast is needed for visibility.
34. Check that focus indicators have at least 3:1 contrast against background because focus must be perceivable.
35. Check that text is not too small below 12px for body because small text harms readability.
36. Check that line height is at least 1.5 times font size because adequate leading improves reading.
37. Check that line length is between 45 and 75 characters per line because long lines reduce comprehension.
38. Check that paragraph spacing is consistent because visual rhythm aids scanning.
39. Check that font family uses system fonts or web fonts with fallback because missing fonts cause fallback issues.
40. Check that font is sans-serif for body text for readability because serif can be harder on screens.
41. Check that text is not justified to avoid rivers because justified text creates uneven spacing.
42. Check that headings use relative units em or rem not px because relative units scale with user preferences.
43. Check that body text uses relative units for scalability because users can resize text.
44. Check that media queries exist for breakpoints at 320px, 768px,
